newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: EU finance ministers leave tough issues to leaders.
newsitem.headline: EU finance ministers leave tough issues to leaders.

text.p: European Union finance ministers on Friday agreed a plan to keep government budgets sound after the introduction of a single currency but the toughest details were left to EU leaders meeting later in the day.
The agreement came after nearly 11 hours of crisis talks dogged by German insistence on watertight guarantees that countries would be punished if they allowed excessive deficits.
Irish Finance Minister Ruairi Quinn, who chaired the meeting, said EU leaders would have to agree figures to define when countries with excessive deficits would be exempt from fines.
At issue was a proposal to fine countries in a single currency that let their deficits grow beyond three percent of gross domestic product.

The leaders would be asked to consider whether countries could be exempt from fines if their economies contracted by 1.5 percent. Countries could make special pleas for leniency if their economies fell by less than that but the cut-off would be 0.75 percent, according to the proposal.
Some ministers were optimistic the leaders would reach agreement. French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said there was no reason why they should not.
